sections.description:
Short title and commencement

BALOCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
BALOCHISTAN
LOCAL GOVERNMENT (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1999
An Ordinance further
to amend Balochistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980
[Gazette of
Balochistan, Extraordinary, 19th July, 1999]
No. Legis.2-30/LAW/75-II, dated
19-7-1999.--The following Ordinance made by the Government of Balochistan op
13th July, 1999, is hereby published for general information:--
1. Short title and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the Balochistan
Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1999.
(2) It shall come into force at
once.

3. Amendment of section 16 of
Ordinance II of 1980.‑‑In the said Ordinance, for section 16,
the following shall be substituted:‑‑
"16. Election of Chairman
and Vice‑Chairman.‑‑(1) For every Local Council, except
Municipal Corporation, there shall be a Chairman and a Vice- Chairman.
(2) For every Municipal
Corporation, there shall be a Mayor and a Deputy Mayor.

mentioned in subsections (1) and (2) above shall be elected in the prescribed

sections.shortTitle: Baluchistan Local Government Second Amendment Ordinance 1999
sections.description:
Amendment of section 17 of Ordinance II of 1980

BALOCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
BALOCHISTAN
LOCAL GOVERNMENT (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1999
An Ordinance further
to amend Balochistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980
[Gazette of
Balochistan, Extraordinary, 19th July, 1999]
No. Legis.2-30/LAW/75-II, dated
19-7-1999.--The following Ordinance made by the Government of Balochistan op
13th July, 1999, is hereby published for general information:--
4. Amendment of section 17 of
Ordinance II of 1980.--In the said Ordinance, after subsection (2) of
section 17, the following new subsection shall be added, namely:--
"(3) Every nomination shall
be made by a separate nomination paper in the prescribed form on solemn
affirmation made and signed by the candidate, accompany--
(i) a declaration that he has
consented to the nomination and that he fulfils the qualifications and is not
subject to any of the disqualifications being elected as a member;
(ii) a declaration that no loan,
obtained from Government any bank, financial institution, cooperative society
or corporate body in his own name or in the name of his spouse or dependent
children or dependent parents or any business concern mainly owned by the
aforesaid, remains unpaid on due date and he has not defaulted the payment of
loan;
(iii) a declaration that he, his
spouse or dependent children or dependent parents or a business concern mainly
owned by the aforesaid have not made any default in payment of taxes or
Government dues and utility expenses including telephone, electricity, gas and
water charges etc.
Explanation-I.--For the
purposes of utility expenses the following information shall be submitted:--
(i) Telephone number(s).
(ii) Account numbers of Gas and
Electricity.
(iii) Complete addresses of
immovable properties, hired or rented or owned or shared.
Explanation-II.--The required
information shall be in respect of nominee, his spouse, dependent parents and
children and business concern mainly owned by any of them.
(iv) a statement specifying his
educational qualifications, occupation, National Identity Card Number and date
of birth/age;
(v) a statement of assets and
liabilities of his own, spouse and dependents on the prescribed form as on the
preceding thirtieth day of June;
(vi) an assurance that he shall
abide by the Code of Conduct issued by the Election Authority;
Explanation.--For the
purpose of this section the expression--
(a) "loan" shall mean
the loan, advance credit or finance obtained;
(b) "mainly owned"
shall mean holding or controlling or majority interest in a business concern;
(c) "taxes" includes
all taxes levied by Federal, Provincial or Local 'Authorities;
(d) "Government dues"
includes rent charges of rest houses or lodges owned by the Federal Government,
Provincial Government, Local Authorities or Corporations established or
controlled by such Governments."

sections.shortTitle: Baluchistan Local Government Second Amendment Ordinance 1999
sections.description:
Insertion of new section 18-A in Ordinance II of 1980

BALOCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
BALOCHISTAN
LOCAL GOVERNMENT (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1999
An Ordinance further
to amend Balochistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980
[Gazette of
Balochistan, Extraordinary, 19th July, 1999]
No. Legis.2-30/LAW/75-II, dated
19-7-1999.--The following Ordinance made by the Government of Balochistan op
13th July, 1999, is hereby published for general information:--
5. Insertion of new section 18‑A
in Ordinance II of 1980.‑‑In the said Ordinance after section
18, the following new sections shall be added, namely:‑‑
" 18‑A.‑‑Assistance
to Election Authority.‑‑It shall be the duty of all the executive
authorities in the Federation, in the Province and all Local Authorities under
the administrative control of Federation and Province to assist the Election Authority
in the performance of its functions as may be required of their by the Election
Authority or its member or Officer authorised by the Election Authority.
18‑B.‑‑Suspension
of Officer.‑‑(1) The Election Authority may at any time, for
reasons to be recorded in writing, suspend any officer performing the functions
of the Returning Officer, Assistant Returning Officer, Presiding Officer,
Assistant Presiding Officer, Polling Officer, Delimitation Officer, Assistant
Delimitation Officer or any other public functionary assisting such Officer or
any member of the Police force or other law enforcing agency who obstruct or
prevent or attempts to obstruct or prevent the conduct of fair and impartial
polls or influence or attempts to interfere viz. an elector when he records his
vote or influence in any manner the polling staff or an elector or does any
other act calculated to influence the result of an elector and make such
arrangements as it may consider necessary for the performance of the functions
of the officer so suspended.
(2) Where the Election Authority
proceeds against any person under subsection (1), it shall refer the matter to
the appropriate authority for taking disciplinary action against such person.
18‑C.‑‑Contempt
of Election Authority.‑‑Any proceedings before the Election
Authority including its Chairman or members independently shall be deemed to be
a judicial proceedings within the meaning of section 228 of the Pakistan Penal
Code, 1860, and the Election Authority' shall be deemed to be a Court within
the meaning of sections 476 and 480 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1898.
"

BALOCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
BALOCHISTAN

An Ordinance further
to amend Balochistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980
[Gazette of

No. Legis.2-30/LAW/75-II, dated
19-7-1999.--The following Ordinance made by the Government of Balochistan op
13th July, 1999, is hereby published for general information:--
6. Substitution of section 20
of Ordinance II of 1980.‑‑In the said Ordinance, for section
20, the following shall be substituted:‑‑
"20. Qualification
of candidates and members.‑‑A person shall be qualified ~to be a
candidate and a member of the Local Council if‑‑
(a) he is a citizen of Pakistan;
(b) he is not less than twenty‑five
years of age and is enrolled as a voter in any electoral roll of any local area
within the limits of Local Council in which the seat falls:
Provided that persons
hereinbefore elected shall not be deseated being less than 25 years of age.
(c) he is of good character and
is not commonly known as one who violates Islamic Injunctions;
(d) he has not been convicted for
a crime involving moral turpitude or for giving false evidence, and .
(e) he has not, after the
establishment of Pakistan, worked against the integrity of the country or
opposed the Ideology of Pakistan:
Provided that the
disqualifications specified in clause (c) shall not apply to a person who is a
non‑Muslim, but such a person shall have good moral reputation.

sections.shortTitle: Baluchistan Local Government Second Amendment Ordinance 1999
sections.description:
Substitution of section 21 of-Ordinance II of 1980

BALOCHISTAN LOCAL GOVERNMENT
BALOCHISTAN
LOCAL GOVERNMENT (SECOND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1999
An Ordinance further
to amend Balochistan Local Government Ordinance, 1980
[Gazette of
Balochistan, Extraordinary, 19th July, 1999]
No. Legis.2-30/LAW/75-II, dated
19-7-1999.--The following Ordinance made by the Government of Balochistan op
13th July, 1999, is hereby published for general information:--
7. Substitution of section 21
of‑Ordinance II of 1980.‑‑In the said Ordinance, for
section 21, the following shall be substituted:‑‑
"21.‑‑Disqualification
of candidates and members.‑‑(1) A person shall be disqualified
from being elected as, and from being, a member of a Local Council, if‑‑
(a) he ceases to be a citizen of
Pakistan or acquires the citizenship of foreign State, or
(b) he is an undischarged
insolvent, or
(c) he is of unsound mind and has
been so declared by a competent Court, or
(d) he has submitted any false or
incorrect declaration or statement, in any material on nomination form; or
(e) he is a guarantor of any Loan
in default.
(f) he is a salaried official of
the Federal Government or a Provincial Government or of a public or statutory
Corporation, a Local Council or other Local authority; or
(g) has been, on conviction for
an offence involving moral turpitude, sentenced to imprisonment for a term of
not less than six months; or
Explanation.‑‑Moral
turpitude means anything that injures the moral fibre of a person and lowers
him down in moral values.
(h) he has been dismissed from
the service of Federal Government or a Provincial Government or of public or
statutory corporation on the ground of misconduct, unless a period of two years
has not elapsed since his dismissal, or
(j) he has in the service of
Federal Government or Provincial Government or of any statutory body or anybody
which is owned or controlled by the Government or in which the Government has a
controlling share or interest, unless a period of one year has not elapsed
since he ceased to be in such service, or
(k) he is found guilty of a
corrupt or illegal practice under any law for the time being in force, unless a
period of two years has elapsed from the date on which that order takes effect,
or
(l) he has been removed or
compulsorily retired from the service of Federal Government, Provincial
Government or of a public or statutory corporation, on the ground of misconduct
unless a period of two years has not elapsed since his removal or compulsory
retirement; or
(m) he is a retired servant of
the Federal Government or the Provincial Government or of a public or statutory
corporation, a Local Council or other local Authority unless one year has
elapsed from the date of such retirement; or
(n) he is under contract for work
to be done or goods to be supplied to any of the Local Council with the
District or has otherwise any pecuniary interest in its affairs; or
(o) he is disqualified from the
membership of any elective body under any law for the time being enforce; and
(p) he has been or is engaged
directly or indirectly in subversive or anti‑Stale activities or
propagating any opinion or acting in any manner prejudicial to the Ideology of
Pakistan or the sovereignty, integrity or security of Pakistan.
Explanation.‑‑Anti‑State
activities shall include instigation to students, labour or any other section of
people with a view to promote lawlessness or disorder.
(2) No order passed under
subsection (1) shall be called in question in any Court.

BALOCHISTAN

An Ordinance further

17. Amendment of section 39 of
Ordinance II of 1980.‑‑In the said Ordinance, for subsection
(2) of section 39, the following shall be substituted as under: ‑‑
"(2)(a) All meetings of a
Council shall ordinarily be presided over by its Chairman, and in his absence
by a Vice‑Chairman, or a Member chosen for that purpose by the members
present at meeting:
Provided that meeting in which no
confidence motion is moved against the Chairman or Vice‑Chairman, or an
Election is held to any of such office bearers, shall be presided over by such
person or officer, as may be prescribed.
(b) Every meeting of a Council
shall be open to the public, unless the person presiding the meeting orders
that the proceedings or any enquiry or deliberation before the Council should
be in camera:
Provided that the person
presiding the meeting may, at any time, cause any person to be removed who
interrupts the proceedings or does not obey its ruling,,. "
